text: Decode with SSD streaming drains (cudaDeviceSynchronize) after every layer because queue_layers requires !g->streaming. The mid-layer selected readback (blocking hipMemcpy, null stream) already orders all prior GPU work before any expert-cache eviction/upload, so the end-of-layer drain is redundant except at the Engram layer and the last layer. Skipping it overlaps next-layer attention launches with MoE execution. Expected: a decode gain of several percent, bit-identical logits.

DS4_ROCM_V41_STREAM_QUEUE=1 + DS4_ROCM_V41_SHARED_FIRST=1 (opt-in): frontier logits bit-exact and generated text identical (8K gen128 x8 runs, 32K gen64 x6 runs). Decode gain small: 8K ABBA4 stream-queue alone mean +2.5 percent (per-pair +7.1/+1.8/+1.1/+0.1), 32K ABBA3 both flags +0.9 percent (all pairs >=0). Prefill unaffected. The 11.6 ms host_drain was mostly overlapped GPU work. Runs in findings/v41-stream-queue/runs.txt

Long-context prefill: the wide indexer head GEMM (FP32 Tensile MT32x32 SgemmStridedBatched + per-head scratch + reduce kernel) dominates late chunks. Q and keys are FP4xpow2 per 32-block, so a fused FP16-WMMA kernel with per-block power-of-two normalization computes exact block dots, keeps the head reduction order, writes no scratch. Expected: bit-identical scores and a prefill gain growing with context. Opt-in DS4_ROCM_V41_INDEX_WMMA=1.

DS4_ROCM_V41_INDEX_WMMA=1 (int8 WMMA, per-32-block pow2 normalization, exact int64 block combine): 64K frontier logits bit-exact in 2 ABBA pairs, generated text identical; prefill 171.50/170.66 -> 188.81/188.68 tps (+10.3 percent). In-model check mode found 0 score mismatches vs FP32 GEMM on 32 sampled calls; an earlier FP16-WMMA version was inexact (FP16 WMMA accumulation not exact for mixed-sign sums) and failed the 64K gate.

120K frontier (ctx 131072, 92GB cache), stock defaults vs STREAM_QUEUE+SHARED_FIRST+INDEX_WMMA=1(packed, 32-row tiles)+INDEX_FP4: prefill 142.72 -> 166.93 tps (+17 percent), logits bit-exact, generated text identical (32 tokens). Decode 11.41 -> 11.14 tps, single pair, within run noise: no decode gain shown at 120K.

Faster fused scorer (queries pre-normalized once to int8, no per-head LDS/barriers, int32 exact-combine fast path): 120K frontier all flags prefill 182.46 tps vs stock 142.72 (+28 percent, single run each, same session), logits bit-exact vs stock, generated text identical. Decode 11.08 vs 11.41 tps, within noise.

DS4_METAL_V41_DECODER_SUFFIX=1 on top of the exact flags: prefill 24K prose/code/docs 202.5/196.6/188.8 -> 311.4/312.5/307.5 tps, 120K prose 182.5 -> 380.1 tps. Not bit-exact: frontier max_abs 0.80/0.36/0.40 (24K), 0.67 (120K); argmax equal and top-k set equal at 24K on all three prompts; 128-token greedy text identical for docs, diverges after ~half for prose and code (plausible continuations). No decode penalty beyond run noise. Mathematically equivalent computation (layers 20-39 rows outside the sliding-window tail are never consumed); drift is MMQ row-block rounding (findings/codex-suffix-decision.md).

User directive (2026-11-06): every change with a gain and no regression becomes default. Promoted on ROCm, each with a =0 escape hatch: DS4_ROCM_V41_INDEX_WMMA (fused int8 WMMA indexer, packed keys), DS4_ROCM_V41_INDEX_FP4 (packed decode keys), DS4_ROCM_V41_STREAM_QUEUE, DS4_ROCM_V41_SHARED_FIRST. Default-binary check at 32K gen 64: logits bit-exact vs stock, text identical, all batch scoring on the fused kernel. Decoder suffix stays opt-in (changes outputs) pending user decision.

Decoder suffix made ROCm default (DS4_METAL_V41_DECODER_SUFFIX=0 disables) with new DS4_ROCM_V41_SUFFIX_MIN_ROWS=4096: layers 20-39 compute at least their last 4096 rows so the post-prefill expert-cache seed sees enough routes (plain suffix left 778 slots empty, decode misses 557 vs 321, decode -11 percent). 24K prose gen128 ABBA2: decode 10.86 (off) vs 11.26 (on), prefill 199 -> 308 tps. Long-prefix (16384) perplexity on 512 scored tokens off -> on: prose 4.0458 -> 4.0224, code 1.1247 -> 1.1250, docs 2.7488 -> 2.7542 (mixed sign, rounding-level). Runs in findings/v41-decoder-suffix/decode-ab.txt.

Decode, all ROCm default, each =0 disables, bit-exact (frontier logits + identical 128-token text in every run): (1) DS4_ROCM_V41_ENGRAM_ASYNC: the 2x24 per-token Engram disk rows are read concurrently by a persistent 16-thread pool and awaited only at layer 1; (2) DS4_ROCM_V41_Q8_DECODE_ROUND: single-row Q8 GEMV rounds to bf16 in its epilogue, removing ~80 launches/token; (3) DS4_ROCM_V41_PTRS_ZERO_COPY: the decode expert pointer table lives in coherent mapped host memory, removing 3 H2D copies + cross-stream event per layer (a ~53 us copyBuffer stall, 2.1 ms/token of GPU time). 24K gen128 ABBA3 (1)+(2)+(3) off vs on: 11.39 -> 11.74 tps (+3.1 percent, 3/3). (4) DS4_ROCM_NORM_BATCHED: RMS norm loads batched 8 ahead with the same accumulation order (unit-tested bit-identical, 16.6 -> 4.7 us for n=20480); ABBA3 11.68 -> 11.85 tps (+1.5 percent, 3/3). 96GB cache: misses 827 -> 765 per 512 tokens, decode unchanged; kept 92GB.

DS4_ROCM_V41_NORM_FUSE (ROCm default, =0 disables): one-launch [bf16(x)]->rms_norm->bf16(out) (unit-tested bit-identical), hc_expand_split with bf16 store + the 16-byte pre<-split copy folded in, q_a/kv pair rounding folded into the norms, grouped output_a GEMV rounds in its epilogue. ~490 fewer launches/token (1923 kernels/token after). 24K gen128 ABBA3: 11.90 -> 12.05 tps (+1.3 percent, 3/3), logits bit-exact, text identical in all 6 runs.

Decode indexer scorer on int8 WMMA (heads as the M dimension, packed keys, exact block combine, reference head order): DS4_ROCM_V41_INDEX_DECODE_WMMA (ROCm default, =0 disables). In-model check DS4_ROCM_V41_INDEX_DECODE_CHECK=1: 64/64 calls 0 score mismatches vs the scalar kernel at 24K. 120K gen64 ABBA2: decode 11.25 -> 11.90 tps (+5.8 percent), text identical in all 4 runs; the scalar kernel cost 5.4 ms/token at 120K. Prefill in these runs ~365 tps at 120K (stock 142.7).
Spinning on the selected-id readback event instead of a blocking wait would remove a host wake-up gap seen after the shared expert in a 120K decode trace.

reason: Neutral: 24K gen128 ABBA3 blocking 12.01 vs spin 11.99 tps; 120K gen64 ABBA2 11.90 vs 11.99 with one negative pair. The 110 us trace gap was profiler-inflated. Kept opt-in (DS4_ROCM_ASYNC_READ_SPIN=1), default off.

text: Cold prefill is SSD-read-bound (24K: 145 GiB read, 37 s of 79 s waiting; KIOXIA EXCERIA BASIC DRAM-less NVMe: 4.9 GB/s with 8 MB sequential reads, ~2 GB/s achieved with 16 concurrent workers). Read workers sweep, cold 8K prefill: 1:214 2:228 3:229 4:231 8:220 16:202 18:197 tps. All 4 workers costs decode (-2.6 percent, misses lose parallelism), so DS4_ROCM_STREAM_LAYER_READ_WORKERS=4 (default) caps only large batches (prefill layer loads, >18 jobs); decode miss batches keep 16. 8K gen256 ABBA3: prefill 205.9 -> 227.5 tps (+10.5 percent, 3/3), decode 12.43 -> 12.35 (-0.6 percent, within noise but 3/3 lower), bit-exact. A warm server reuses cached experts in prefill (layer reuse) and reads less.
Seeding the post-prefill expert cache from whole-prompt routing frequencies (plus last-chunk recency) instead of the last chunk only would cut early-decode misses.

reason: 24K gen128: misses 284 (last chunk, 4096-row suffix tail) vs 278 (whole prompt): ~2 percent, not worth the code. Reverted.

text: Keep the decoder suffix default: official V4.1 quality gate (score_official, 20260911-long manifest, 9 prompts 8/16/32K) off vs on: avg NLL +0.27 percent (0.6937 -> 0.6956), case wins 4/5, first-token 8/8 both, greedy LCP equal, API top1 85.76 -> 85.59 percent. Rounding-level, in band. Scores: findings/v41-quality/long-*.tsv and long-suffix-compare.txt.

A decode Q8_0 GEMV using wide coalesced loads (lanes read contiguous 16-byte spans of the row and dequantize in registers) gets closer to the 128-bit read ceiling than the per-block byte-load blocks4 kernel. It changes FMA order (rounding-level), so it is gated by the official V4.1 quality scorer.

reason: Standalone gfx1151 benchmarks vs v41_q8_f32_blocks4 (205-228 GB/s on 35-53 MB matrices): LDS-staged 128-bit row copy 145-196 GB/s and not bit-identical; lane-per-block wide unaligned loads 107-188 GB/s; fully repacked aligned SoA layout with int4 loads 173-227 GB/s (no gain). Pure streaming reads reach ~242 GB/s with 128-bit loads, but a GEMV also re-reads the activation vector from cache; ~225 GB/s is the practical GEMV ceiling here. The decode GEMVs are at it.
